PerformanceTrendsResult.description:
What `analyze_performance_trends` answers with.

One shape covers all seven of the handler's returns. Six of them are
degenerate — no activities, an unknown metric, too few points to regress,
a regression that failed — and differ from the real answer only in
carrying no `statistics`. Making that one field optional says exactly
that, where seven variants would have said it six times.

insights.description: Plain-language readings of the trend, always at least one.

statistics.description: The regression itself. Absent when `trend` reports why there is none.

timeframe.description: The window requested, echoed back: week, month, quarter or year.

trend.description:
`improving`, `stable` or `declining` when the regression ran; otherwise
why it did not — `no_data`, `invalid_metric`, `needs_more_data`,
`insufficient_data` or `calculation_error`.

TrendStatistics.description: The linear regression behind a performance trend.

confidence.description:
Confidence in the trend. The same number as `r_squared`: the fit is
what the confidence is, and both names are on the wire already.

correlation.description: Pearson correlation between the metric and time.

end_value.description: Last value in the window; absent when the window was empty.

moving_average_7day.description: Mean of every point in the window, for comparison against the fit.

p_value.description:
Significance of the slope. Absent when the regression could not
produce one — too few points for the t-distribution to be defined.

percent_change.description:
Change from first to last as a percentage. Absent when there are fewer
than two points, or the first value was zero and the ratio undefined.

r_squared.description: Share of variance the line explains, 0 to 1.

slope.description: Change in the metric per day.

standard_error.description: Standard error of the slope estimate.

start_value.description: First value in the window; absent when the window was empty.

tools.name: analyze_training_load
tools.description: Analyze training load from per-activity TSS (the provider's own figure, else estimated from power against the FTP saved with set_physiology, from heart rate against the threshold heart rate saved there — measured, else estimated from the lactate threshold and max HR — or from pace or duration). Returns CTL (fitness), ATL (fatigue) and TSB (form), form as a percentage of CTL with its band, weekly TSS totals and a taper reading.

provider.description: Fitness provider to query (e.g., 'strava'). Defaults to configured provider.

sleep_provider.description: Optional sleep provider (e.g., 'whoop', 'garmin'). When given, last night's sleep score, duration and HRV are returned as recovery context beside the load; the load numbers themselves do not change.

FormBand.description:
Descriptive band for an athlete's form, expressed relative to their own
chronic load (`form_pct = tsb / form_ctl * 100`) per the TrainingPeaks/Friel and
intervals.icu convention.

Form on a day is the previous day's CTL minus ATL, and it is a share of
that same previous day's CTL (Coggan/TrainingPeaks, see [`TrainingLoad`]).
A band is therefore built from a whole [`TrainingLoad`] or
[`DailyTrainingLoad`], which carry both numbers from the same day, never
from a TSB and a CTL handed over separately.

The bands state the magnitude of fatigue relative to fitness. They are not
injury predictions: fixed-threshold injury prediction from load ratios is
not supported by the literature (Impellizzeri et al., 2020). This is the
single form vocabulary — every surface that bands form derives it from
here rather than comparing raw TSB to a constant, because the same TSB is
a normal build week at CTL 120 and the deepest fatigue at CTL 40.

oneOf.description: No chronic base to normalize against — form is not interpretable.
Form below -30% of CTL: the deepest fatigue band.
Form -30% to -20% of CTL: the deep end of the productive zone.
Form -20% to -10% of CTL: the normal fatigue of a productive block.
Form -10% to +5% of CTL: neither fatigued nor peaked.
Form +5% to +20% of CTL: fresh, ready for quality work or racing.
Form above +20% of CTL: risk of detraining.

FormInterpretation.description:
What every form-bearing payload says about its own numbers.

One type rather than a `json!` per surface: this is the shared key that
stops `get_training_history` and `analyze_training_load` describing the
same number two different ways (registre#199). A tool declaring an
outputSchema needs it typed, not just consistent.

deep_fatigue_is_not_overtraining.description:
That a deeply negative reading is the expected signal in a planned
overload block, not evidence of overtraining.

form_band.description: The bands, their edges, and that they are not an injury prediction.

method.description:
How the numbers were computed, so an agent can answer "how do you
calculate this" from the payload instead of admitting it cannot.

tsb.description: What TSB is, and why the raw number is not the thing to read.

tsb_pct_of_ctl.description:
What form relative to the athlete's own fitness means, and what a
null one means.

atl.description: Acute training load — recent fatigue, at the end of today.

ctl.description: Chronic training load — long-run fitness, at the end of today.

form_ctl.description: CTL at the end of yesterday — the fitness `tsb` is a share of.

tsb.description:
Training stress balance — form today: CTL minus ATL at the end of
yesterday, so today's session moves `ctl`/`atl` but not this.

tsb_pct_of_ctl.description:
Form as a percentage of `form_ctl`, which is how the band is decided.
`None` when that CTL is too small to divide by.

weekly_tss.description: Weekly TSS totals across the window, oldest week first.

LoadRecoveryContext.description: The sleep side of a load reading.

hrv_available.description:
Whether the night carried an HRV reading at all — distinct from
`hrv_rmssd` being absent, which could also mean the provider omitted
it from a night it did return.

hrv_rmssd.description: RMSSD in milliseconds, when the provider reported one.

recovery_status.description: The analyser's word for that score.

sleep_provider.description: The sleep provider that supplied the night.

NoTrainingLoad.description: The answer when there is no load to report.

message.description:
Which of the two cases this is — no activities at all, or too little
history for the calculator to produce a load.

providers_used.description:
Which providers were asked. Present on the empty answer too: "we
looked at Garmin and found nothing" and "we looked at nothing" are
different answers, and the athlete is entitled to tell them apart.

ProvidersUsed.description:
The providers behind an answer, named so a client can say where a number
came from rather than implying one source.

activity_provider.description: The provider the activities came from.

sleep_provider.description: The sleep provider, when one was asked for and answered.

tools.name: calculate_daily_nutrition
tools.description: Calculate daily calorie and macronutrient needs based on biometrics and goals. For an athlete with a medical/PAR-Q flag on file it returns qualitative `guidance` and `figures_withheld` instead of any amount, because their clinician sets those.

activity_level.description: Activity level: sedentary, lightly_active, moderately_active, very_active, extra_active

training_goal.description: Training goal: maintenance, weight_loss, muscle_gain, endurance_performance

tools.name: calculate_fitness_score
tools.description: Calculate a fitness score (0-100) from chronic training load (40%), consistency, the share of weeks with three or more activities (30%), and pace improvement (30%), over the period chosen with `timeframe`; omitted, it scores the last 30 days. Chronic training load scores each session against the FTP and threshold heart rate saved with set_physiology, as analyze_training_load does. A named `sleep_provider` adds a sleep-based adjustment.

provider.description: Fitness provider to query. Defaults to configured provider.

sleep_provider.description: Optional sleep provider (e.g., 'whoop', 'garmin'). When given, last night's sleep quality adjusts the score: up to +5% for excellent recovery, down to -10% for poor.

timeframe.description: How far back to score consistency and pace progression: 'month' (the last 30 days), 'quarter' (90), 'year' (365), or 'all_time' (every activity fetched). Set it to the period the athlete named — omitted, this scores 30 days and cannot answer a question about three months or a season. Chronic training load is a current-state number and is computed from the full fetched history regardless of this setting.

consistency_score.description: Share of weeks with three or more sessions. Weighted 30%.

performance_score.description: Pace improvement across the window. Weighted 30%.

FitnessLoadMetrics.description: The training-load numbers behind the CTL component, rounded.

tsb.description:
Training stress balance — form today: CTL minus ATL at the end of
yesterday.

activities_analyzed.description: How many activities were in the window.

components.description: The three weighted parts of the score.

fitness_score.description: The score, 0 to 100, rounded to a whole number.

fitness_score_unadjusted.description:
The score before the recovery adjustment, present only when one ran.
Both numbers ship so a client can show what sleep cost or bought.

history_span_days.description:
Days of history the chronic training load was computed from — always the
full fetched span, never the window. Stated so a reply names the period
it analysed instead of inferring one (registre#415).

level.description: Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Elite or Very High.

metrics.description: The training-load numbers the CTL component came from.

providers_used.description: Which providers the answer was built from.

recovery_adjustment.description:
The sleep-derived adjustment, present only when a sleep provider was

trend.description: Whether the score is rising, flat or falling across the window.

window_days.description:
Days the score's consistency and pace components cover, or `null` when

recovery_adjustment.description:

tools.name: calculate_personalized_zones
tools.description: Calculate training zones from the athlete's own measurements, falling back to their saved physiology for anything not supplied here. Zone families whose inputs are unknown are listed under `unavailable` instead of being estimated; `input_sources` says where each number came from.

ftp.description: Functional Threshold Power in watts. Omit to use the athlete's saved value; power zones are omitted when neither exists.

lactate_threshold.description: Lactate threshold as a fraction of VO2 max (0.65-0.95), used for pace zones: threshold pace runs at the speed whose oxygen cost is that share of VO2 max. Omit to use the athlete's saved value, else Daniels' threshold intensity, 0.88 (named in `input_sources`).

max_hr.description: Maximum heart rate in bpm. Omit to use the athlete's saved value, or the estimate from their saved age by the configured max-HR algorithm (algorithm.maxhr).

resting_hr.description: Resting heart rate in bpm. Omit to use the athlete's saved value.

vo2_max.description: VO2 max in ml/kg/min. Omit to use the athlete's saved value; pace zones are omitted when neither exists.

min_hr.description:
Lower bound in bpm: inclusive for zone 1, exclusive above it (each
zone opens where the one below it closes).

name.description:
What the zone is called (cageux's zone names), so a client need not
map numbers to names.

HeartRateZones.description:
The athlete's heart-rate zones under cageux's `VO2max`-tiered Karvonen
model: five zones, and a sixth for an athlete whose tier carries one.

tier.description: The `VO2max` tier that chose the zone fractions.

vo2_max_source.description:
Whether the `VO2max` that chose the tier was supplied (`provided`) or
estimated from the maximum and resting heart rate
(`heart_rate_ratio`, Uth 2004).

zone_6.description:
Anaerobic, up to the maximum heart rate. Null when the athlete's
tier has no zone 6 (`VO2max` below 50) or their zone 5 already ends at
their maximum.

HrZoneModel.description: Which model cut a stored set of heart-rate zones.

oneOf.description:
Five zones at fixed fractions of heart-rate reserve, written before
the zones moved to cageux. Only ever read from an old row; nothing
writes it.

HrZoneTier.description:
An athlete's `VO2max` tier, which selects the heart-rate reserve fractions
their zones are cut at

This is a cut on measured or estimated `VO2max`, not the athlete's declared
experience ([`crate::models::FitnessLevel`]): a self-described beginner
with a `VO2max` of 55 gets the advanced tier's zones.

oneOf.description: `VO2max` from 50 up to 60 ml/kg/min: zone 6 becomes available
`VO2max` of 60 ml/kg/min or more: the narrowest bands

PaceZone.description:
One pace zone, as `m:ss` per kilometre.

Strings rather than seconds: these are for an athlete to read off, and the
numbers they are derived from are already in `zone_calculations`.

PaceZones.description: The Daniels VDOT pace zones, named for what they are for.

zone_1_easy.description: Easy running: 59-74 % of velocity at `VO2max` by default.

zone_2_marathon.description: Marathon pace, cut from threshold pace.

zone_3_threshold.description: Threshold pace, around the athlete's lactate threshold.

zone_5_neuromuscular_max_pace.description:
Neuromuscular (repetition) work: the slowest pace of the zone, which
runs on to any faster pace, as `m:ss` per kilometre.

PersonalizedZones.description:
The zones that could be derived from what the athlete supplied.

Each is null when its inputs were missing, and `unavailable` on the result
says which input would unlock it. Substituting a default here would hand
an athlete zone boundaries computed from somebody else's physiology.

ftp.description: The FTP the power zones were built from, echoed back.

heart_rate_zones.description: Needs both a resting and a maximum heart rate.

max_watts.description:
Upper bound in watts, inclusive. Null for level 7, which Coggan
leaves open-ended.

min_watts.description:
Lower bound in watts: 0 for level 1, exclusive above it (each level
opens where the one below it closes).

name.description: The level's name (cageux's Coggan level names).

PowerZones.description: Coggan's seven power levels, as fractions of FTP.

Vo2maxSource.description: Where the `VO2max` that chose an athlete's tier came from

oneOf.description: The caller supplied it (a lab test, a field test, a device estimate)
Estimated from maximum and resting heart rate (Uth et al. 2004)

ZoneCalculations.description: How the heart-rate zones were derived, and the two threshold heart rates.

aerobic_threshold_hr.description: Aerobic threshold heart rate (75 % of the reserve), in bpm.

lactate_threshold_hr.description:
The lactate threshold heart rate the model places (85 % of the
reserve), in bpm — the reference of these zones. Training load scores
against the athlete's own `threshold_hr`, saved with `set_physiology`.

method.description:
Always `karvonen_vo2max_tiered`: cageux's heart-rate-reserve zones with
fractions chosen by the athlete's `VO2max` tier.

tier.description: The `VO2max` tier that chose the fractions.

vo2_max_source.description: Whether that `VO2max` was supplied or estimated from the heart rates.

ZoneInputProfile.description:
The inputs the zones were derived from, as resolved.

Every one is optional because the athlete may have supplied none of them:
the tool reports what it had rather than substituting a default, which is
why `unavailable` on the result exists at all.

ftp.description: Functional threshold power in watts — what the power zones need.

lactate_threshold.description:
Lactate threshold as a fraction of `VO2max` — what places threshold
pace in the pace zones. Daniels' 0.88 when none is measured, which
`input_sources` then names `daniels_default`.

max_hr.description: Maximum heart rate in bpm. With `resting_hr`, this gives the HR zones.

vo2_max.description: `VO2max` in ml/kg/min — what the pace zones need.

outputSchema.description: What `calculate_personalized_zones` answers with.

input_sources.description:
Where each input came from, keyed by field name: `provided`, `profile`,
`estimated_from_age` for a maximum heart rate estimated by the
configured max-HR algorithm (named under `max_hr_algorithm`), or
`heart_rate_ratio` for a `VO2max` estimated from the heart rates to
choose the zone tier, or `daniels_default` for a lactate threshold
none was measured for. An athlete should be able to tell a measured
number from an estimated one.

personalized_zones.description: The zones that could be derived.

unavailable.description: For each zone that could not be derived, which input would unlock it.

zone_calculations.description: How the heart-rate zones were computed. Absent when they could not be.

outputSchema.title: PersonalizedZonesResult

tools.name: calculate_recovery_score
tools.description: Calculate a holistic recovery score combining training stress, sleep and HRV. Fetches sleep and activities from connected providers automatically and computes CTL, ATL and TSB from those activities against the thresholds saved with set_physiology (FTP, threshold heart rate, max and resting heart rate, weight).

activity_provider.description: Provider to fetch activities for training load (strava, garmin, coros, whoop, intervals_icu, terra). Omit to auto-select

recent_hrv_values.description: Array of recent HRV values (RMSSD, ms)

sleep_data.description: Manual sleep data, used instead of a provider fetch when no sleep_provider is named. Fields: date (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339) and duration_hours (required), deep_sleep_hours, rem_sleep_hours, light_sleep_hours, awake_hours, efficiency_percent, hrv_rmssd_ms, resting_hr_bpm, provider_score

sleep_provider.description: Read only this source's synced sleep (whoop, garmin, intervals_icu). Omit to merge every connected source's sleep per night

DataCompleteness.description: Data completeness indicator for recovery scoring

oneOf.description: All data sources available (TSB + Sleep + HRV)
Some data sources available (TSB + Sleep, or TSB + HRV)
Excellent recovery (low fatigue, ready for high intensity)
Good recovery (moderate fatigue, ready for moderate intensity)
Fair recovery (elevated fatigue, easy training only)

components_available.description: Number of components used in calculation

sleep_score.description: Sleep quality score (0-100), None when in TSB-only mode

RecoveryProvidersUsed.description:
Which providers the recovery score was assembled from.

Recovery is cross-provider by design: activities from one, sleep and HRV
from another. Naming both is what lets an athlete tell a low score from a
missing feed.

activity_provider.description: Where the training data came from.

sleep_provider.description:

tools.name: compose_route
tools.description: Join stretches found by discover_routes into one itinerary, drawn as a single line and measured along it. Call it when the session you propose runs along more than one discovered route — the riverside path out, the rail trail on — or comes back the way it went. Pass `route_refs` in running order and `out_and_back: true` for an aller-retour. Stretches are joined only where they meet on the ground, within 30 m: each must meet the next, which is what a route's `connects_to` lists. A wider gap is refused rather than bridged, because a straight line across it may cross water, a fence or a road; the refusal names the two stretches that do not meet, so drop one, reorder them, or put a stretch that connects them in between — never propose a refused itinerary anyway. Returns one `route_ref` for the whole line and `distance_meters`: that is the distance to quote, never a sum you work out from the stretches. To show the itinerary, name that `route_ref` in a `dravr-viz` route block with `source_tool` "compose_route" — never write coordinates. A route_ref is kept for 24 hours: an unknown or expired one means calling discover_routes again. Elevation and surface are not known here either: never describe the itinerary as flat or hilly on the strength of this tool.

out_and_back.description: True to come back the same way to the start (an aller-retour): the line is drawn out and back, and the distance returned covers both ways. Defaults to false.

route_refs.description: The route_ref of each stretch, in running order, from 1 to 8: each one a route_ref that discover_routes (or an earlier compose_route) returned in this conversation. Each stretch must physically meet the next — a route's connects_to lists the ones it meets.

items.description: A route_ref, such as "rt_3f9a0c41d27b8e65", copied as it was returned.

ComposedStretch.description: One stretch of a composed route.

name.description:
The stretch's name: the trail's name in OSM, or a composed route's
stretch names joined in running order.

route_ref.description: The stretch's own reference, as it was passed.

outputSchema.description: What `compose_route` answers with.

distance_meters.description:
Length of the composed line in metres, rounded, measured along the
line itself and doubled for an out-and-back: the distance to quote,
never a sum of the stretches' own distances.

joins_meters.description:
Metres of unmapped ground crossed at each join, rounded: one per pair
of consecutive stretches, each at most 30.

out_and_back.description: Whether the route returns along itself to where it started.

The reference the composed line is kept under for 24 hours. To show

whose `source_tool` is `compose_route`; it can also be passed back to
`compose_route` as one stretch of a longer itinerary.

outputSchema.title: ComposeRouteResult

tools.name: compute_training_history
tools.description: Compute and persist Endurance daily training-state rollups for the authenticated user across the requested window — CTL, ATL, TSB (Coggan), acute:chronic load balance, monotony + strain (Foster), ramp rate, and daily TSS load. Use this to seed the `training_history` table on first use, after a long gap in syncs, or when the user asks for a specific historical window. Default window is the last 90 days.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window (ISO date YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 90 days before `to` when omitted.

to.description: Inclusive end of the window (ISO date YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today in the athlete's own timezone.

outputSchema.description:
What `compute_training_history` answers with.

A write tool that reports its own scope. The window is echoed because the
caller may have passed none and taken the default, and `rows_upserted` is
how an agent knows whether the recompute actually had days to work with —
zero is a valid answer for a window the athlete did not train in.

`from` is the window actually computed, which is later than `requested_from`
when stored history could not warm the whole ask. Both are reported because
`ctl`/`atl`/`tsb` are plain floats seeded at zero: a day computed without its
CTL warm-up behind it carries a chronic load that is wrong low and looks
exactly like a real one, so the agent has to be told which days exist rather
than inferring it from a row count.

complete.description: Whether every requested day was backed by enough stored history.

What the agent may and may not claim when coverage fell short. `None`
when the whole window was computed.

requested_from.description:
First day the caller asked for, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Differs from `from`
when stored history was too shallow to warm the whole window.

rows_upserted.description: How many daily rows were written or overwritten.

to.description: Last day of the window, inclusive.

tools.name: discover_routes
tools.description: Discover real named running, cycling, hiking, or ski routes near a location, grounded in OpenStreetMap data via the Overpass API, around a `place` (preferred) or `latitude`/`longitude`. Use this whenever the user asks you to propose, suggest, or find a route, trail, or outdoor session in a specific area. Never invent street names, trail names, or terrain you have not verified via this tool. Returns up to 20 named routes, nearest first, each with coordinates and a measured `distance_from_center_meters` — quote that distance rather than estimating one from the coordinates. Signed itineraries and trails are listed ahead of paved connectors. `distance_meters` says what it measures in `distance_source`: `mapped_geometry` is the longest connected run of fetched ways carrying the name — a lower bound, since the trail can continue past it; `osm_tag` is the length declared for the whole route, of which only part may lie inside the radius. A signed route with no declared length has none. When the session has a distance, pass it as `target_distance_meters`; each route then carries `target_fit` (`single_pass`, `out_and_back` or `repeats`) and `passes_for_target` — tell the athlete plainly when a route needs an out-and-back or repeats. Elevation, surface and how flat or uninterrupted a route is are NOT returned: never describe a route as flat, hilly or suited to intervals on the strength of this tool. An empty list means OSM has no named route in that radius: widen `radius_meters` or say so plainly, never substitute a name you did not read here. For ski queries this reads OSM piste:type data (same source as OpenSkiMap). A route whose line is mapped carries a `route_ref`: to show the athlete that stretch, name it in a `dravr-viz` route block with `source_tool` "discover_routes" — never write coordinates. It also carries `connects_to`, the `route_ref`s of the other routes here that it physically meets. To propose an itinerary over several stretches, pass their refs in running order to `compose_route`, each meeting the next, and quote the distance it returns.

latitude.description: Latitude of the search center, in decimal degrees. Only used when `place` is NOT set. Example: 45.87 for Prévost, Québec.

longitude.description: Longitude of the search center, in decimal degrees. Only used when `place` is NOT set. Example: -74.08 for Prévost, Québec.

place.description: Place to search around, resolved by the same gazetteer as get_weather_forecast. Prefer this over latitude/longitude. Give the place's own name, optionally followed by its region and country to choose among places of the same name: 'Prévost, Quebec, Canada', 'Saint-Alexis-des-Monts' or 'Mont-Tremblant'. Write the region out: an abbreviation such as 'QC' chooses nothing. When set, the latitude/longitude parameters are ignored.

radius_meters.description: Search radius around the resolved center, in meters. Clamped between 500 and 50000. Defaults to 10000 (10 km).

sport_type.description: What kind of route to look for. One of: 'run', 'trail_running', 'ride', 'mountain_bike', 'gravel_ride', 'ebike_ride', 'hike', 'walk', 'cross_country_skiing', 'alpine_skiing', 'backcountry_skiing', 'snowshoe'. Defaults to 'run'; a name that is no sport is refused.

target_distance_meters.description: Distance of the session the route is for, in meters (15000 for a 15 km run), between 500 and 500000. When set, routes whose length lands within a tenth of it — in one pass or one out-and-back — lead the list, and each route says whether it covers the distance in a single pass, an out-and-back, or repeats. Omit it to get the nearest routes regardless of length.

DiscoveredRouteEntry.description:
One route as `discover_routes` reports it.

Grounded in OpenStreetMap, which is why so much is optional: a way tagged
by a volunteer may carry a name and nothing else.

connects_to.description:
The `route_ref`s of the other routes in this answer whose mapped line
physically meets this one's: an end of either within 30 m of the
other. A `compose_route` itinerary joins only stretches that meet, so
chain stretches along these links, in running order. Absent when the
route meets none of the others.

difficulty.description: Difficulty as the source grades it; absent when ungraded.

distance_from_center_meters.description: How far the route is from the search centre, in metres, rounded.

distance_meters.description:
Length in metres, rounded; absent when it is unknown — a route
relation with no declared length, or a way with neither geometry nor
one.

distance_source.description:
What `distance_meters` measures. `mapped_geometry`: the longest run
of fetched ways carrying this name that join end to end — a stretch
that exists on the ground and a lower bound on the trail, which can
continue past it. `osm_tag`: the length the mapper declared for the
whole route, however little of it lies inside the search radius.

latitude.description: Latitude of the route start or centre.

longitude.description: Longitude of the route start or centre.

passes_for_target.description:
How many times the route is covered — 1, 2 for an out-and-back, more
for repeats: the fewest passes that reach the target to within a
tenth. Present with `target_fit`.

route_ref.description:
The handle this route's mapped line is kept under for 24 hours: `rt_`
and 16 hex digits. Present when the line is mapped and stored, which
is what lets the route be drawn: name it as `route_ref` in a
`dravr-viz` route block whose `source_tool` is `discover_routes`, or
pass it to `compose_route` to join this stretch with others into one
itinerary. Absent for a route with no mapped line (`osm_tag` or no
length), which no map can draw.

route_type.description: What kind of route it is, lowercased: cycling, hiking, ski.

source.description: Which dataset it came from, lowercased.

target_fit.description:
How the route covers the target distance: `single_pass` (as long as
the target, or short of it by no more than a tenth), `out_and_back`

tools.name: estimate_lactate_thresholds
tools.description: Locate the athlete's lactate thresholds from a step test they report — each stage's power in watts or pace in seconds per kilometre, its blood lactate in mmol/L, and heart rate if a strap was worn. Returns LT1 by the log-log breakpoint and LT2 by modified Dmax, Dmax and the 4.0 mmol/L convention, each under its own name with the intensity, lactate and heart rate at that point; the lactate band table from 1.0 to 4.0 mmol/L; and power zones anchored on the modified-Dmax LT2 when the stages are in watts. Call it when the athlete reports a test such as '200 W 1.1, 225 W 1.4, 250 W 2.3, 275 W 4.1 mmol'. Needs at least four stages, each harder than the last. This only estimates: to keep a threshold, call set_physiology with ftp_watts or threshold_pace_sec_per_km, and threshold_hr for its heart rate, after the athlete confirms it.

items.description: One stage of the step test.

heart_rate.description: Heart rate at the end of the stage in bpm, when a strap was worn. Omit otherwise.

intensity.description: The stage's intensity in the test's unit: watts, or seconds per kilometre for a running pace.

lactate_mmol.description: Blood lactate sampled at the end of the stage, in mmol/L.

unit.description: How every stage's intensity is expressed — watts for power, seconds_per_km for a running pace.

BandRow.description: One row of the lactate band table.

heart_rate.description: Heart rate there, when the stages carried one.

intensity.description: The intensity the fitted curve puts it at.

lactate_mmol.description: The concentration this row is for.

CurveFit.description: The curve that was fitted to the stages.

model.description: The model, written out, so the coefficients mean something.

r_squared.description:
How much of the variance the fit explains. A low value is the signal
that the located points should not be trusted.

heart_rate.description:
Heart rate there. Explicitly null when no strap was worn, so a reader
can tell "measured and absent" from "not part of this answer".

intensity.description: Watts or seconds per kilometre at the located point.

marks.description: What that method marks, in words.

LactatePowerZones.description: Coggan's power levels cut from the modified-Dmax LT2, or why there are none.

anchor.description:
Always `lt2_modified_dmax` — named so a client cannot mistake these
for zones anchored on a different construct.

ftp_watts.description: The threshold the zones were built on.

reason.description: Why not: the stages were paces, or the anchor could not be located.

Upper bound in watts, inclusive. Null for level 7, which Coggan
leaves open-ended.

min_watts.description:
Lower bound in watts: 0 for level 1, exclusive above it (each level
opens where the one below it closes).

name.description: The level's name (cageux's Coggan level names).

PowerZones.description: Coggan's seven power levels, as fractions of FTP.

StoredThresholds.description: What the athlete's profile already holds on these axes.

max_hr.description: Stored maximum heart rate, when one is set.

threshold_hr.description: Stored lactate threshold heart rate, when one is set.

threshold_pace_sec_per_km.description: Stored threshold pace, when one is set.

anyOf.description: The method located a point.
It could not, and says why.

ThresholdReport.description:
One construct's verdict: either a located point or the reason there is
none.

Two arms rather than one shape with optionals, because the two answers
carry disjoint keys — a determined threshold has `intensity`,
`lactate_mmol` and `heart_rate`, an undetermined one has `reason`, and
neither set is a subset of the other. A client can therefore tell them
apart from the payload alone, and `heart_rate` stays explicitly null on a
determined point rather than vanishing: "the strap was not worn" and
"this method found nothing" are different facts.

UndeterminedThreshold.description: A threshold the method could not locate.

marks.description: What that method marks, in words.

reason.description: Why the method could not locate a point on these stages.

band_table.description:
Intensity and heart rate at each lactate concentration from 1.0 to

curve_fit.description: The cubic that was fitted, and how well it fitted.

framing.description:
How to talk about these numbers. Carried on the payload because a

LT2 three ways: modified Dmax, Dmax, and the 4.0 mmol/L convention.
A list rather than three keys because they are the same question

Coggan's seven power levels anchored on the modified-Dmax LT2, when

tools.name: estimate_vo2max
tools.description: Estimate the athlete's VO2max in ml/kg/min from a field test they describe — a Cooper 12-minute run distance, a Rockport timed mile walk with finishing heart rate, an Astrand-Ryhming steady-state ride at a known power, a hard-versus-easy pace ratio, a VDOT they already know, or a race or time trial they ran (its distance and time). Call it when the athlete reports a test result such as 'I ran 2.8 km in 12 minutes' or 'I walked a mile in 13 minutes and my heart rate was 140'. Body weight and age come from the stored profile when not restated, and the result says which inputs were defaulted. This only estimates: to keep the number, call set_physiology with vo2_max after the athlete confirms it.

max_speed_ms.description: from_pace: the fastest speed in metres per second the athlete can hold for 3–8 minutes.

power_watts.description: astrand_ryhming: the steady power held on the ergometer, in watts.

recovery_speed_ms.description: from_pace: the athlete's easy or recovery speed in metres per second.

time_seconds.description: rockport_walk: seconds taken to walk one mile (1,609 m) as fast as possible. race_result: the finishing time in seconds (19:30 is 1170).

vdot.description: from_vdot: the VDOT value, 30–85. It is already VO2max in ml/kg/min, so this reports it after range-checking.

weight_kg.description: Body weight in kilograms. rockport_walk and astrand_ryhming need it; when omitted the stored profile weight is used.

What `estimate_vo2max` answers with.

Which inputs were taken from the stored profile rather than given in

formula.description: The equation used, named so the number is auditable.

implied_threshold_pace_sec_per_km.description:
The threshold pace this estimate implies, in seconds per kilometre —
the running pace at the share of velocity-at-`VO2max` the training
zones config states, which is what `set_physiology` stores as
`threshold_pace_sec_per_km`. Absent when the estimate does not give a
usable velocity.

saved.description: Always false: this tool estimates, it does not write.

stored_vo2_max.description:
The `VO2max` already on the profile, for comparison. Absent when none

to_store.description: What to do with the number once the athlete confirms it.

vo2max_ml_kg_min.description: The estimate, in ml/kg/min, rounded to one decimal.

tools.name: export_dossier
tools.description: Export the Endurance 'dossier.json' aggregate for the authenticated user — physiological profile (VO2max, FTP, threshold pace, fitness level, critical power, W′, critical speed, D′), HR + power zones, goals and nutrition slots — composed at read time from the underlying tables. Critical power, W′, critical speed and D′ each carry `kind` (measured or estimated) and `origin`: quote an estimated value as an estimate attributed to its origin ('Vekta estimates your CP at 312 W'), never as a measurement. An FTP, threshold or max heart rate, or threshold pace a provider supplied is named in `threshold_provenance` with its origin: quote it as that provider's estimate ('intervals.icu has your FTP at 285 W'); one not named there is the athlete's own. Empty slots come back as `null` rather than 404, so agents can rely on the shape.

AerobicThresholdPace.description:
An athlete's aerobic-threshold (LT1) running pace, estimated from their
threshold (LT2) pace

Esteve-Lanao et al. (2026) measured both ventilatory thresholds in 1,411
trained runners (819 men, 592 women, mean age about 37, at least a year of
structured training and three sessions a week) on a treadmill at 1 % grade,
speed rising 0.3 km/h every 30 s to exhaustion, gas exchange by Cosmed K5,
VT1 and VT2 by the Davis criteria read by three evaluators. Speed at VT1
was 84.4 ± 4.7 % of speed at VT2 (men 84.1 ± 4.5, women 84.8 ± 4.9), with
little change across fitness levels.

The ratio is of *speeds*, so the pace is divided by it:
`lt1_pace = threshold_pace / ratio`. A 240 s/km threshold gives
240 / 0.844 = 284.4 s/km.

# Limits

- A descriptive group mean, not a regression: one athlete's ratio spreads
  about ±4.7 points around it, which is ±14 s/km at a 4:00/km threshold.
  [`Self::faster_bound_sec_per_km`] and [`Self::slower_bound_sec_per_km`]
  carry that ±1 SD range.
- VT2 (the respiratory compensation point) from a 30-second-step ramp is
  not identical to the athlete's stored threshold pace, which is usually a
  roughly one-hour race pace or a lactate-threshold field test; the two sit
  close but VT2 can be slightly faster, which would put this estimate a
  little fast.
- Trained runners on a treadmill only: the ratio is for running pace, not
  for cycling power or other sports.

cohort.description: The group the ratio came from

faster_bound_sec_per_km.description: LT1 pace at the ratio's mean plus one SD: the faster end (s/km)

slower_bound_sec_per_km.description: LT1 pace at the ratio's mean minus one SD: the slower end (s/km)

threshold_pace_sec_per_km.description: The threshold (LT2) pace the estimate starts from (s/km)

AerobicThresholdPower.description:
An athlete's aerobic-threshold (LT1) cycling power, estimated from FTP

`watts = ftp_watts x power_ratio`, the study's VT1/VT2 power ratio. A
250 W FTP gives 164 W by Pallarés et al. (2016) and 149 W by Benítez-Muñoz
et al. (2025), against the 188 W the top of Coggan's endurance level
(75 % of FTP) would claim.

# Limits

- FTP stands in for the second threshold. Jeffries et al. (2021) found FTP
  level with the 4 mmol/L lactate power in trained cyclists but with wide
  limits of agreement, so the estimate inherits that spread.
- Each ratio is of group means, not a per-rider regression; `note` says so
  for each.

# Scientific References

- Pallarés, J.G., Morán-Navarro, R., Ortega, J.F., Fernández-Elías, V.E. &
  Mora-Rodriguez, R. (2016). "Validity and Reliability of Ventilatory and
  Blood Lactate Thresholds in Well-Trained Cyclists." *`PLoS` One*, 11(9),
  e0163389. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0163389
- Benítez-Muñoz, J.A., Alcocer-Ayuga, M., Cupeiro, R. et al. (2025).
  "Ventilatory Thresholds Differences According to Aerobic Fitness Level in
  1450 Males and 241 Females on Cycle-Ergometer: A Cross-Sectional Study."
  *Eur J Sport Sci*, 25(7), e12323. doi:10.1002/ejsc.12323
- Jeffries, O., Simmons, R., Patterson, S.D. & Waldron, M. (2021).
  "Functional Threshold Power Is Not Equivalent to Lactate Parameters in
  Trained Cyclists." *J Strength Cond Res*, 35(10), 2790-2794.

ftp_watts.description: The FTP the estimate starts from (watts)

lower_watts.description:
LT1 power at the study's lowest group ratio (watts), when it reports
more than one group

method.description: The study whose ratio was applied

upper_watts.description:
LT1 power at the study's highest group ratio (watts), when it reports
more than one group

AerobicThresholdPowerMethod.description:
The published cycling ratio an aerobic-threshold (LT1) power estimate uses

Both are VT1/VT2 power ratios from graded cycle tests, applied to FTP on
the assumption that FTP sits at the second threshold. Neither study
measured FTP; no study found measures LT1 power beside FTP in the same
riders (Jeffries et al. 2021 and Valenzuela et al. 2018 compare FTP with
second-threshold markers only).

oneOf.description: Pallarés et al. (2016): VT1 200 ± 36 W, VT2 304 ± 39 W in 14 well-trained men
Benítez-Muñoz et al. (2025): VT1 and VT2 power in 1,450 men and 241 women

DossierFact.description:
A single pillar-context fact projected onto the dossier.

This is a read-time projection of a `pierre_memory::UserFact` — the subset
the per-user OKF bundle needs to render, plus a computed freshness flag.
`kind` and `source` are carried as their stable string slugs to keep this
type free of a `pierre-memory` dependency. The `object` field is
user-authored free text and must be treated as untrusted at render time.

object.description: The athlete's own words — UNTRUSTED user free text, in their language.

predicate_code.description:
`PredicateCode` slug (e.g. `training_for`, `parq_yes`, `states`): what
the fact says. The sentence is rendered per locale by the consumer.

stale.description: Computed at compose time: `valid_until` is in the past.

updated_at.description: When the fact was last touched.

oneOf.description: Intermediate athlete (2-4 years experience, local competition)

HrZoneModel.description: Which model cut a stored set of heart-rate zones.

oneOf.description:
Five zones at fixed fractions of heart-rate reserve, written before
the zones moved to cageux. Only ever read from an old row; nothing
writes it.

HrZoneSet.description:
Heart-rate zone boundaries for a single user.

Each `zN_max` is the upper bound (inclusive) of zone `N` in beats per
minute; zone `N+1` starts above it. `z6_max` is present when the athlete's
tier carries a zone 6 (`VO2max` of 50 or more and a zone 5 that stops
short of their maximum), and is then their maximum heart rate.

This is distinct from
[`pierre_core::models::HeartRateZone`](super::HeartRateZone), which carries
per-activity time-in-zone counts. `HrZoneSet` is the per-user definition;
`HeartRateZone` is the per-activity occupancy.

model.description:
Which model cut these boundaries. A row written before this field
existed reads as [`HrZoneModel::Legacy`].

tier.description: The `VO2max` tier that chose the zone fractions; absent on a legacy row.

vo2_max_source.description:
Whether the `VO2max` that chose the tier was the athlete's own or
estimated from their heart rates; absent on a legacy row.

z1_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 1 (recovery) in bpm.

z1_min.description:
Lower bound of Zone 1 (recovery) in bpm, inclusive: the zone's floor
on the athlete's reserve. Absent on a legacy row.

z2_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 2 (endurance) in bpm.

z3_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 3 (tempo) in bpm.

z4_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 4 (threshold) in bpm.

z5_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 5 (`VO2max`) in bpm.

z6_max.description:
Upper bound of Zone 6 (anaerobic) in bpm, the athlete's maximum heart
rate; absent when their zones have no zone 6, and on a legacy row.

HrZoneTier.description:
An athlete's `VO2max` tier, which selects the heart-rate reserve fractions
their zones are cut at

This is a cut on measured or estimated `VO2max`, not the athlete's declared
experience ([`crate::models::FitnessLevel`]): a self-described beginner
with a `VO2max` of 55 gets the advanced tier's zones.

oneOf.description: `VO2max` from 50 up to 60 ml/kg/min: zone 6 becomes available
`VO2max` of 60 ml/kg/min or more: the narrowest bands

MeasurementKind.description:
Whether a physiological value was measured or estimated.

This is what decides how the value may be framed. A measured critical
power is "your CP is 312 W"; an estimated one is "Vekta estimates your CP
at 312 W", never stated bare. Where the value came from is a separate axis
([`MetricProvenance::origin`]): a provider can hand over either kind.

oneOf.description:
Produced by a named test: a lab protocol, a 3-minute all-out test, a
set of time trials fitted to the model, a track test.

Produced by a model from training data (a provider's or an app's), or
stated by the athlete without naming the test behind it.

MetricProvenance.description: Where a physiological value came from and how much it can be trusted.

as_of.description: The day the value was measured or estimated, when known.

kind.description: Measured or estimated — the framing axis.

origin.description:
Who produced it: a provider (`vekta`, `intervals.icu`), a test (`lab`,
`3-min all-out test`), or `athlete-reported`. The attribution an
estimate is quoted with.

PhysiologicalSex.description:
An athlete's physiological sex, as the published equations use it.

Keytel et al. (2005) take it for exercise energy expenditure, and
Esteve-Lanao et al. (2026) give sex-specific VT1/VT2 speed ratios for the
aerobic-threshold pace.

It selects an equation's coefficients and nothing else. It is recorded
only when the athlete states it or a provider reports it, never inferred
from a name or anything else; absent, every reader falls back to the
pooled or sex-free form, or reports that it needs it.

oneOf.description:
Five zones at configurable FTP percentages, written before the zones
moved to cageux. Only ever read from an old row; nothing writes it.

Power zone boundaries for a single user (cycling / running power).

Each `zN_max` is the upper bound (inclusive) of zone `N` in watts, rounded
to the watt. Zone 7 is everything above `z6_max` and has no upper bound;
a legacy row holds only five zones and no `z6_max`.

Which model cut these boundaries. A row written before this field

z5_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 5 (`VO2max`) in watts.

z6_max.description:

(neuromuscular power) is everything above it. Absent on a legacy row.

SportType.description:
Enumeration of supported sport/activity types

This enum covers the most common fitness activities across all providers.
The `Other` variant handles provider-specific activity types that don't
map to the standard categories.

oneOf.description: Other activity type not covered by standard categories

ThresholdEstimate.description:
The dossier's LT1 / LT2 anchors, each read from where it lives rather
than re-derived here.

- **LT1** (aerobic threshold) heart rate is cageux's
  [`HrZones::aerobic_threshold_bpm`], 75 % of the athlete's heart-rate
  reserve; LT1 power is cageux's [`AerobicThresholdPower::estimates`]
  from the FTP, one per published VT1/VT2 power ratio, each with its note.
- **LT2** (lactate threshold) heart rate is the athlete's LTHR (measured,
  else estimated from their lactate threshold), else cageux's
  [`HrZones::lactate_threshold_bpm`], 85 % of reserve; LT2 power is the
  FTP and LT2 pace the saved threshold pace.
- **LT1 pace** is cageux's [`AerobicThresholdPace`] from the saved
  (running) threshold pace: the VT1/VT2 speed ratio of Esteve-Lanao et al.
  (2026), with its one-SD bounds and the cohort the ratio came from: the
  men's or women's ratio when the athlete's sex is saved, the pooled one
  otherwise.

An anchor whose inputs are missing is absent: the heart-rate anchors need
the athlete's zones (a saved resting and maximum heart rate), the power
anchors an FTP, the pace anchor a threshold pace.

lt1_hr.description:
Aerobic threshold heart rate in bpm: 75 % of the athlete's heart-rate
reserve.

lt1_pace.description:
LT1 pace estimated from that threshold pace (Esteve-Lanao et al.
2026), with the faster and slower bound one SD of the ratio either
side and the cohort. Absent without a saved threshold pace, or when it
lies outside the 120-600 s/km running range the estimate covers.

lt1_power.description:
LT1 power estimated from the FTP, one entry per published VT1/VT2
power ratio (Pallarés et al. 2016, then Benítez-Muñoz et al. 2025).
Each carries its watts, the ratio, the study's range when it reports
one, and a `note` on what it rests on: quote LT1 power as these
estimates with their notes, never as one measured number. Absent
without a saved FTP.

lt2_hr.description:
Lactate threshold heart rate in bpm: the athlete's LTHR, else 85 % of
their heart-rate reserve.

lt2_pace_sec_per_km.description: LT2 pace (sec/km): the saved threshold pace.

ThresholdProvenance.description:
Where each of the profile's four scalar thresholds came from, for the ones
a provider supplied.

A threshold with no entry here is the athlete's own. That covers every
value stored before provenance was recorded and every value
`set_physiology` writes. An entry is written only by an import from a
provider, always [`MeasurementKind::Estimated`] with the provider as its
origin and the day the provider's setting last changed: the framing is
"intervals.icu has your FTP at 285 W", never a bare "your FTP is 285 W".
An import refreshes only an entry its own origin wrote, so a value the
athlete set is never replaced.

ftp_watts.description: Where the functional threshold power came from.

max_hr.description: Where the maximum heart rate came from.

threshold_hr.description: Where the lactate threshold heart rate came from.

threshold_pace_sec_per_km.description: Where the threshold pace came from.

ThresholdRatioCohort.description: Which of the study's groups the VT1/VT2 ratio was taken from

oneOf.description: All 1,411 runners, used when the athlete's sex is unknown

UserPhysiologicalProfile.description:
User physiological profile for personalized analysis

Contains physiological data used for calculating personalized heart rate zones,
pace zones, and other performance thresholds based on individual fitness metrics.

critical_power_watts.description:
Critical power in watts: the asymptote of the hyperbolic power-duration
relationship, the highest power sustained without a steady drain of
[`Self::w_prime_joules`]. Always carries whether it was measured or
estimated, and by whom.

critical_speed_mps.description:
Critical speed in metres per second: the running and swimming analogue
of critical power.

d_prime_meters.description:
D′ (D prime) in metres: the finite distance capacity above critical
speed.

ftp_watts.description:
Functional Threshold Power in watts (cycling / running power).

Drives Endurance power-zone derivation, intensity-factor
computation, and the polarized-distribution analytics in
`latest.json`. `None` until the athlete supplies it (manually or
via a 20-min FTP test).

hr_zones.description:
Heart-rate zone boundaries.

Per-user definition stored alongside the profile. Distinct from
the per-activity `HeartRateZone` (which carries time-in-zone for
a single activity).

lactate_threshold_percentage.description:
Lactate threshold as a fraction of `VO2max`, 0.65-0.95: the share of
aerobic capacity the athlete sustains at threshold (fractional
utilisation — about 0.60 untrained, 0.75-0.90 trained, Joyner & Coyle
2008). Places threshold pace in the VDOT pace zones and, when no
[`Self::threshold_hr`] is measured, estimates the LTHR
([`Self::lactate_threshold_hr`]).

power_zones.description:
Power zone boundaries (cycling / running power).

Same shape as [`Self::hr_zones`] but for watts. `None` for
athletes without a power meter or saved FTP.

sex.description:
Physiological sex, for the published equations that take one
([`PhysiologicalSex`]). Set by the athlete with `set_physiology`, or
filled once from a provider that reports it when none is set; a value
the athlete set is never replaced by a provider's.

threshold_hr.description:
Lactate threshold heart rate (LTHR) in bpm, as measured — a 30-minute
field test, a ramp test or a lab report. Heart-rate-based training
stress is scored against it.

threshold_pace_sec_per_km.description:
Threshold pace in seconds per kilometre.

Used by the running-side equivalent of FTP to derive Endurance
pace zones and intensity factor for runs without a power meter.
`None` until the athlete supplies it.

threshold_provenance.description:
Where [`Self::ftp_watts`], [`Self::threshold_hr`], [`Self::max_hr`]
and [`Self::threshold_pace_sec_per_km`] came from, for the ones a
provider supplied: each such value is that provider's estimate, quoted
with its origin ("intervals.icu has your FTP at 285 W"). A threshold
not listed is the athlete's own. Serialized with the profile — the
dossier and every tool that echoes the profile carry it — and left out
when every threshold is the athlete's own, so a profile no import
touched reads exactly as before.

vo2_max.description: VO2 max in ml/kg/min (if measured or estimated)

w_prime_joules.description: W′ (W prime) in joules: the finite work capacity above critical power.

Vo2maxSource.description: Where the `VO2max` that chose an athlete's tier came from

oneOf.description: The caller supplied it (a lab test, a field test, a device estimate)
Estimated from maximum and resting heart rate (Uth et al. 2004)

outputSchema.description:
What `export_dossier` answers with.

The composed dossier with the estimated lactate thresholds alongside it.
The dossier is flattened in rather than nested, which is what this tool
has always sent.

`threshold_estimate` is always present, empty when nothing is known.
That is the dossier's own "empty slots, not 404" contract: an agent reading
the payload can tell "no FTP on file" from "this tool does not report
thresholds", and a key that appears only sometimes cannot.

goals.description:
Active goals (e.g. race target, weekly volume, weight). Free-form
JSON until the typed goals model lands; the Endurance payload
surfaces them as-is so agents can read them.

hr_zones.description:
Heart-rate zone definitions.

`None` until `set_physiology` derives them, which it does as soon as
both a resting and a maximum heart rate are on the profile.

medical.description:
Medical / PAR-Q flags the agent must heed. Gated separately from pillar
facts so raw medical detail can be withheld per privacy policy.

north_star.description:
The user's North Star — one to three core life motivations orienting the
pillars. Rendered as the index of the OKF bundle.

nutrition.description:
Nutrition snapshot (preferences, dietary restrictions, hydration
targets). Free-form JSON; `None` when the user has not configured
nutrition.

physiology.description:
Physiological profile slot (FTP, threshold pace, fitness level, etc.).

`None` until a profile is written. Two tools write
`user_physiological_profiles`, both in the athlete's own context:
`set_physiology`, whose values are the athlete's own, and
`import_provider_thresholds`, which fills a threshold from a provider
only when the profile has none or the value is that provider's earlier
one. Each imported threshold is named in the profile's
`threshold_provenance`.

pillars.description:
Per-user pillar context: durable facts grouped by health pillar. Empty
until the user has answered onboarding or accumulated conversation facts.
`BTreeMap` keeps JSON/markdown rendering order deterministic.

power_zones.description:
Power zone definitions (cycling / running power).
`None` for athletes without a power meter or saved FTP.

threshold_estimate.description:
LT1/LT2 heart rate, power and pace read off the profile — heart rate
at 75 % / 85 % of the athlete's reserve unless an LTHR is saved, FTP
and two published LT1 power estimates for power, the saved threshold
pace and its LT1 estimate for pace. Gives the dossier training zone
anchors even when the athlete has measured none directly.

outputSchema.title: DossierExport

tools.name: export_intervals
tools.description: Export the Endurance 'intervals.json' shape for a single activity — one row per lap with avg HR, normalized power, intensity factor, and decoupling. Use this when a coach needs the per-interval breakdown for tempo/threshold/VO2max workouts. Activities without laps return a single synthetic interval covering the whole session.

activity_id.description: Provider activity id to analyse (e.g. Strava activity id as string).

IntervalRow.description: One row in `intervals.json` representing a single lap or interval.

avg_hr.description: Average heart rate (bpm) for this interval.

decoupling_pct.description:
Aerobic decoupling percentage over this interval. `None` when fewer
than 20 paired HR + speed samples are available.

distance_meters.description: Distance in metres. Zero for stationary intervals.

elevation_gain_meters.description: Total elevation gain (m) over the interval.

intensity_factor.description: Intensity factor (`NP / FTP`). `None` when FTP missing or no power.

moving_seconds.description: Moving seconds (excludes stopped time). `None` when provider omitted.

normalized_power.description: Normalized power (Coggan, 30s rolling EMA^4) over this interval.

tools.name: export_latest_snapshot
tools.description: Export the Endurance 'latest.json' snapshot for the authenticated user — per-activity intensity factor, efficiency factor, variability index, aerobic decoupling, and time-in-zone distribution aggregated over a sliding window. Default window is 7 days; pass `window` (1..=365) to change it. Use this when a coach needs a structured per-activity training-state snapshot grounded in the Endurance deterministic-output contract.

window.description: Window length in days (1..=365). Defaults to 7 when omitted.

ActivitySection11Metrics.description:
Per-activity Endurance metrics block.

Each field is `Option<f64>` because the underlying calculation
requires sensor streams (power, HR) that may be missing on a given
activity. Per the Endurance deterministic-output rules, missing
sensor data emits `None` rather than a synthesised estimate.

decoupling_pct.description:
Aerobic decoupling percentage — `(2nd-half HR/speed - 1st-half HR/speed) / 1st-half`.
`None` when the activity has fewer than 20 paired HR+speed samples.

efficiency_factor.description:
Efficiency Factor — `normalized_power / average_heart_rate`.
`None` when either input is missing.

intensity_factor.description:
Intensity Factor — `normalized_power / ftp` (Coggan).
`None` when the activity has no power stream or the user has no FTP.

variability_index.description:
Variability Index — `normalized_power / average_power`.
`None` when the activity has no power stream.

LatestSnapshotActivityRow.description: One row in the per-activity table embedded in the snapshot.

zone_distribution.description:
Time-in-zone distribution computed from the HR stream against the
athlete's [`HrZones`]. `None` when no HR stream is present or the
athlete's zones are unknown (see
[`LatestSnapshot::zone_distribution_unavailable`]).

ZoneDistribution.description:
Time-in-zone distribution computed across one or more activities.

Values are absolute seconds spent in each of the athlete's heart-rate
zones. Sum across all zones plus `above_max_seconds` equals total samples
in the analyzed window. Used by the Endurance `latest.json` payload to
surface polarized-distribution stats (Z1+Z2 share vs Z3 share vs Z4 and up)
to agents.

above_max_seconds.description: Seconds with a heart rate above the athlete's maximum.

z6_seconds.description:
Seconds spent in zone 6 (anaerobic); zero for an athlete whose zones
have no zone 6.

outputSchema.description:
Endurance latest-snapshot payload.

Window-aggregated over the activities passed to
[`build_latest_snapshot`]. Aggregates use simple arithmetic means
across activities that contributed a value (i.e. drop `None`s before
averaging — never substitute zeros).

activities.description: Per-activity rows in chronological order (oldest first).

aggregated_zone_distribution.description: Aggregated time-in-zone distribution across the window.

avg_decoupling_pct.description: Mean decoupling percentage over activities that produced a value.

avg_efficiency_factor.description: Mean efficiency factor over activities that produced a value.

avg_intensity_factor.description: Mean intensity factor over activities that produced a value.

avg_variability_index.description: Mean variability index over activities that produced a value.

total_distance_meters.description: Sum of distances across the activities (metres).

total_duration_seconds.description: Sum of durations across the activities (seconds).

window_days.description: Window length in days that was analysed.

zone_distribution_unavailable.description:
Why the zone distributions are absent when the athlete's heart-rate
zones are unknown: they are cut from a saved resting and maximum
heart rate, never from a default. `None` when the zones were known.

tools.name: export_routes
tools.description: Export the Endurance 'routes.json' shape for a single activity — GPX-derived terrain mix (flat/rolling/climb/steep), elevation gain/loss, and distinct climb segments with Strava-style category. Requires the activity stream to include lat/lon and altitude.

activity_id.description: Provider activity id to analyse (e.g. Strava activity id as string).

Climb.description: One climb segment found inside the route.

category.description: Strava-style climb category (Fiets-style `gain * gradient * 100`).

elevation_gain_meters.description: Total elevation gain over the climb (m).

Endurance terrain mix bucketed by horizontal distance.

The four buckets sum (within rounding) to `total_distance_meters`.

elevation_gain_meters.description: Total elevation gain (positive deltas only) in metres.

elevation_loss_meters.description: Total elevation loss (negative deltas summed as positives) in metres.

gpx_hash.description: SHA-256 hex of the input GPX bytes — used as cache key.

tools.name: extract_activity_streams
tools.description: Return the raw per-second time-series streams for a single activity — heart_rate (bpm), power (watts), cadence (rpm/spm), speed (m/s), altitude (m), and gps_coordinates (lat/lon pairs). Each stream is omitted when the provider didn't record it; a sample the sensor missed is null, never a reading of 0. Use this when a coach needs the underlying samples to rerun a custom analysis the higher Endurance tools (export_intervals / export_routes) don't cover.

activity_id.description: Provider activity id to analyse (e.g. Strava activity id as string).

TimeSeriesData.description:
Time-series data for detailed activity analysis

Every sampled channel is index-aligned with `timestamps`: entry `i` of a
channel is the reading at `timestamps[i]`. A channel that was recorded but
missed a sample (a sensor dropout, a strap that lost contact) carries
`None` at that index — a gap. A gap is not a reading: every consumer in
this crate skips it, so it never enters an average, a zone's time, a
normalized-power window or a decoupling pair, and no provider has to
invent a value (a `0` reads as a real 0 bpm or a real coast) or drop the
whole channel to say a sample is missing. On the wire a gap is `null`; a
channel written before gaps existed (plain numbers) reads unchanged.

cadence.description: Cadence measurements (RPM or steps/min); `None` entries are gaps

distance.description:
Cumulative distance from activity start (meters), one value per entry
of `timestamps` (e.g. Strava's `distance` stream). Read by [`crate::best_efforts::best_efforts`].

heart_rate.description: Heart rate measurements (BPM); `None` entries are gaps

timestamps.description: Time offsets from activity start in seconds

outputSchema.description:
What `extract_activity_streams` answers with.

The provider's raw series, unaggregated. `sample_count` is on the wire
beside them because the series can be long and a caller deciding whether
to ask for it at all should not have to receive it first to find out.

sample_count.description: How many samples each series carries.

streams.description:
Heart rate, power, cadence, GPS and altitude as recorded; a missed
sample is a gap (`null`), never a value.

outputSchema.title: ActivityStreamsResult

tools.name: forget_playbook
tools.description: Delete one learned coaching playbook by id (GDPR forget). The athlete can only forget their own playbooks.

playbook_id.description: The id of the playbook to forget (from list_coaching_playbooks).

outputSchema.description: What `forget_playbook` answers with.

deleted.description:
Rows removed. A COUNT, not a flag: it is 0 when the id was not this
athlete's, which is the same answer as "no such playbook" on purpose —
a caller must not be able to probe another athlete's ids by the shape
of the reply.

playbook_id.description: The id that was asked for, echoed back.

outputSchema.title: ForgetPlaybookResult

tools.name: generate_recommendations
tools.description: Generate personalized training recommendations. The `training_plan`, `recovery` and `all` modes advise on CTL, ATL and TSB scored against the FTP and threshold heart rate saved with set_physiology, as analyze_training_load reports them. In `nutrition` mode, an athlete with a medical/PAR-Q flag on file gets foods and timing with no amount to eat or drink, and `figures_withheld` saying their clinician sets those; the session itself is still described. Calories burned are the device's figure, else Keytel's heart-rate estimate from the saved weight, age and sex; without either, `calories` is null and `calories_unavailable` says why.

provider.description: Fitness provider to query (e.g., 'strava'). Defaults to configured provider.

recommendation_type.description: Type of recommendations to generate: 'all' (default), 'training_plan', 'recovery', 'intensity', 'goal_specific', or 'nutrition'; any other value is refused.

ActivitySummary.description: The session the nutrition advice is about.

calories.description:
Calories burned, rounded: the device's figure, else the Keytel
heart-rate estimate. Null when neither is available.

calories_source.description:
Where `calories` came from: `device`, `keytel_with_vo2max` or
`keytel_without_vo2max`. Null when there is no figure.

calories_unavailable.description: Why there is no calorie figure. Null when there is one.

distance_km.description: Distance in kilometres, rounded, when the activity carried one.

name.description: The activity's name as the provider recorded it.

CorePrinciples.description: The principles the advice is derived from.

intensity.description: How to split hard and easy.

recovery.description: Why rest is where fitness is made.

FigureAuthority.description: Who sets the withheld figures instead of the platform.

FiguresWithheld.description:
The machine-readable statement that figures were withheld, and why.

Present means the athlete has a medical flag on file and the answer carries
no amount to eat or drink: no energy, macronutrient, fluid, sodium or
caffeine intake. What a finished session cost (its calories burned) still
describes the session and is not an intake. Relay `note` rather than
supplying a number of your own.

note.description: What to tell the athlete, in plain words.

reason.description: `medical_flag`: a medical / PAR-Q flag is on file.

set_by.description: `clinician`: who sets these amounts for this athlete.

MacronutrientTargets.description:
Recovery-window targets, scaled to the athlete's stored body weight.

Present only when a body weight is on file: every figure here is per
kilogram in the evidence, so without a weight the recommendations state the
per-kilogram dose instead of inventing a gram count. There is no fluid
target — how much to drink afterwards depends on what the session cost, which
only a before-and-after weigh measures (see the recommendations).

body_weight_kg.description: The stored body weight these were scaled from, kilograms.

protein_g.description:
Protein for the meal or snack after the session, grams: 0.3 g per kg of
body weight (Thomas, Erdman & Burke 2016; Kerksick et al. 2017 give
0.25-0.40 g/kg, or 20-40 g), within about 2 hours.

protein_g_per_kg.description: The per-kilogram protein dose `protein_g` was scaled from.

refuel_carbohydrates_g_per_h_max.description: The high end of that hourly range: 1.2 g per kg per hour.

refuel_carbohydrates_g_per_h_min.description:
Carbohydrate per hour for the first 4 hours, low end, grams: 1.0 g per
kg per hour. Only when the next fuel-demanding session is less than
8 hours away (Thomas, Erdman & Burke 2016); otherwise regular meals
refill glycogen and no hourly target applies.

MealSuggestion.description: One meal, with what it is for.

description.description: What it actually is.

option.description: A short name for the option.

timing.description: When to eat it relative to the session.

RacePredictionSummary.description: Predicted times, when history supports a prediction.

based_on.description: The performance the prediction was derived from, in words.

race_times.description: Predicted times in minutes, keyed by the distance's name.

vdot.description: The athlete's VDOT, the number the paces come from.

RecommendationMetrics.description:
The numbers a recommendation was derived from.

A union across the three modes that report numbers, because the mode is
already named on the parent: `training_plan` fills the schedule and load
fields, `recovery` the load and overtraining fields, `intensity` the
pattern fields. A field that is absent was not measured for that mode.

adequate_recovery.description: Whether the easy days were actually easy enough. `intensity`.

avg_activities_per_week.description: Sessions per week over the window. `training_plan`.

consistency_score.description: How regular those weeks were, 0 to 1. `training_plan`.

hard_percentage.description: Share of sessions that were hard. `intensity`.

hr_drift_detected.description: Whether heart rate drifted upward at a fixed effort. `recovery`.

pattern_detected.description: Whether a hard/easy pattern was found. `intensity`.

risk_level.description:
`low`, `moderate` or `high` — descriptive, never an injury
prediction. `recovery`.

activity_summary.description: The session the nutrition advice is about.

core_principles.description:
The four principles the advice is derived from, quoted so the athlete
can check the reasoning rather than take it.

figures_withheld.description:
Present when the athlete has a medical flag on file: the `nutrition`
mode then answers without `macronutrient_targets`, `meal_suggestions`
or any amount in `recommendations`, because their clinician sets those.

hr_zones_unavailable.description:
Why heart rate did not decide which sessions were hard (`recovery`,
`intensity`, `all`) or how hard the last session was (`nutrition`):
the athlete's heart-rate zones are unknown, so duration and speed
decided instead. Absent when the sessions were read against their
zones, and in the modes that do not read heart rate.

intensity_guidance.description: How to distribute hard and easy work, when the mode is `intensity`.

key_insights.description:
What the numbers say, in prose. Shared by `nutrition` and
`comprehensive`.

macronutrient_targets.description: The macro targets those meals are meant to hit.

meal_suggestions.description: Concrete meals rather than macro targets alone.

metrics.description:
The numbers behind the recommendation. Which of these are filled
depends on the mode — see each field.

periodization_phases.description: The phases of a season, in order.

primary_sport.description: The sport the athlete does most of, when the mode is `goal_specific`.

priority.description: `high`, `medium` or `low`. How much the athlete should act on this.

race_predictions.description: Predicted race times, when there is enough history to predict from.

reasoning.description: Why these recommendations, in the athlete's terms.

recommendation_type.description:
Which mode produced this: `training_plan`, `recovery`, `intensity`,
`goal_specific`, `nutrition` or `comprehensive`. Read this first — it
says which of the optional blocks below to expect. A sampled answer
echoes back whatever mode was asked for.

recommendations.description: The recommendations themselves, most important first.

recovery_actions.description: What to actually do about it.

recovery_status.description: The recovery read, when the mode is `recovery`.

recovery_window.description: The window that matters most after the session.

source.description:
`mcp_sampling` when the client's LLM wrote the prose. Absent means the
deterministic path produced it, which is the distinction an athlete is
entitled to.

suggested_structure.description: A week's shape, when the mode is `training_plan`.

training_summary.description: The training picture the holistic read is built on.

TrainingSummary.description: The training picture behind a comprehensive read.

activities_analyzed.description: How many activities went into it.

ctl.description: Chronic training load, when it could be computed.

intensity_pattern_detected.description: Whether a hard/easy pattern was found at all.

key_workouts.description: The sessions that define the week.

sessions_per_week_max.description: The high end. Equal to the low end when the plan names one number.

sessions_per_week_min.description:
The low end of the session count.

Two numbers rather than one key, because the key used to hold a number
(`3`, `4`) in two branches and a string (`"5-6"`) in a third. One key
with two JSON types cannot be described by any schema, and a client
parsing it as a number silently dropped the busiest athletes' plan.

WithheldReason.description: Why an answer came back without its nutrition figures.

oneOf.description: A medical / PAR-Q flag is on the athlete's dossier.

anyOf.description: `format=json`, the default: the tool's own shape, unchanged.
`format=toon`: the payload rendered as one compact TOON string.

TOON was asked for and could not be produced. The payload still arrives,
as JSON, and says why it is not what was requested — a caller that
silently received JSON would parse it as TOON and fail further away.

format_fallback.description: Always true; present so the fallback is detectable on its own.

outputSchema.description:
A tool payload after the caller's `format` argument has been applied.

Which shape arrives depends on the REQUEST rather than the data, which is
why this is a type rather than three call sites deciding for themselves:
`format=json` sends the tool's own shape, `format=toon` sends a compact
string envelope, and a TOON conversion that fails falls back to JSON while
saying so. Untagged, so the derived schema is an `anyOf` over exactly
those three arms — schemars emits `anyOf` for an untagged enum, not
`oneOf`, so the schema does not itself assert the arms are mutually
exclusive. A client tells them apart by the keys: `toon` and `result` are
the envelope's, and they are fixed rather than per-tool for that reason.

The envelope keys are fixed (`toon`, `result`) rather than derived from a
per-tool `data_key`. A property name that changes per tool cannot be stated
in a schema, so the old `result_toon` / `recipes_toon` / `recipe_toon` /
`results_toon` spelling is gone — the key no longer carries information the
tool name already gives, and the contract is now expressible.
