tools.name: publish_training_plan
tools.description: Publish or discard a group's human coach's draft of a coached athlete's training plan. A coach's save_training_plan for an athlete writes the coach's draft, which the athlete does not see: publish makes it their live plan in one step — the weeks the coach did not draft keep the athlete's own version — and discard throws it away. Call it only when the coach asks to publish or discard. When the athlete's own agent changed a drafted week after the coach drafted it, or re-laid the season, publish is refused with status `conflict` and nothing changes: tell the coach which weeks, and publish again with overwrite_athlete_changes only if they choose to replace the athlete's changes. Publishing does not touch the athlete's calendar; push_training_plan does that afterwards. In a coach's thread about one athlete, `athlete` defaults to that athlete. The caller's own plan has no draft: their saves are already live.

action.description: `publish` makes your draft the athlete's live plan; `discard` throws it away and leaves their plan as it is. One of: publish, discard.

athlete.description: Roster display name of the coached athlete whose plan your draft is of. Only the group's human coach (attached via a coach invite) may set it, for a consenting athlete in a group they coach, and only from a direct chat — never in a room. In the coach's thread about one athlete it defaults to that athlete.

overwrite_athlete_changes.description: Publish over the weeks the athlete's own agent changed since you drafted them, and over a season re-laid under your draft. Set it only after the coach saw the conflicts and chose to replace the athlete's changes. Read only with `publish`.

CalendarPreview.description:
What a push would change, without the entry list.

The save reply reports the counts only: the athlete has just written the
plan and needs to know whether the calendar is behind, not to re-read
every entry they already have.

provider.description: The calendar provider.

pushed_by.description:
Present only when the athlete's human coach, not the athlete, pushes
this calendar (see [`CalendarBlock::pushed_by`]).

CalendarPusher.description: Who puts Dravr's plan on a calendar when it is not the athlete reading it.

oneOf.description:
The athlete's human coach, through the link the athlete reads the
calendar by: only the coach writes it, from Dravr.

CrowdedWeek.description:
One week whose hard sessions sit closer together than its flavour allows.

Named rather than paired for the reason [`WeekReadiness`] is: a tuple
serialises positionally and the reader has to know which slot is which.
The check is flattened, so the kernel stays the one definition of what
"too close" means — including the minimum it applied and which gaps were
short.

oneOf.description: Every gap between hard sessions meets the minimum.
At least one gap is short.

short.description: The short gaps, in date order.

oneOf.description: Fewer than two hard sessions, or no flavour to take the minimum from.

reason.description: Why.

DraftConflict.description: One week the coach drafted whose live version the athlete changed since.

reason.description: Why publishing it would overwrite the athlete's work.

DraftConflictReason.description: Why publishing a drafted week would overwrite the athlete's own work.

oneOf.description:
The athlete's agent saved the week after the coach drafted over it,
or saved it for the first time.

DraftState.description:
Where the coach's open draft stands: which draft it is, when the coach
last saved into it, and what publishing it now would overwrite.

Built only by [`DraftState::of`]. It deserializes too, so a plan card
stored on a reply carries the state it was built with back to the client
unchanged.

conflicts.description:
The drafted weeks the athlete changed since the coach drafted them.
Publishing refuses them unless the coach overwrites them; a week the
coach never drafted is never here.

draft_id.description:
The draft's id: the same through every save until it is published or
discarded.

season_relaid.description:
The athlete's season was re-laid (or laid, or removed) after the draft
began, so the draft's weeks may no longer fit it. Publishing refuses
it unless the coach overwrites it.

updated_at.description: When the coach last saved into the draft.

PlanSafetyReport.description:
What the two safety-shaped checks found in the weeks this save wrote.

A coach's save into their draft of an athlete's plan carries the same
report, measured on the draft view — the draft's outline over the
athlete's live weeks — so the coach hears of it before publishing puts the
plan in the athlete's hands.

The compliance rail has measured every saved week since it shipped and
reported into a log line no agent reads; the readiness rail the same. This
is the half that reaches the turn: the agent sees what the platform
measured on the save it just made, and can say so before the athlete acts
on a week that crowds its hard days or opens well above their recent load.

Only the two checks the ledger calls safety-shaped travel here. Time in
zone, volume against target and template parameter ranges are coaching
judgements the agent already owns, and a platform that volunteered those
would be second-guessing the plan rather than flagging a risk.

Structured, never prose. What the athlete is told is the agent's to write:
the framing rules on load ratios are CI-enforced and live in the prompt,
so a sentence composed here would be a second place they could be broken.

Absent when both checks read within, unmeasured, or had nothing to measure
— which is the common case and costs the turn nothing.

crowded_weeks.description: Weeks whose hard sessions are closer together than the minimum.

ramp.description:
The opening week against the athlete's recent weekly hours, when it
came in above the threshold. `None` when it did not, or when there was
no baseline to compare against.

PublishStatus.description: What `publish_training_plan` did with the coach's draft.

oneOf.description: The draft is the athlete's live plan.

Nothing was published: the athlete's plan changed under the draft.
`conflict` names what collided.
The draft was thrown away; the athlete's plan is as it was.

PushPreview.description:
What a push would do, judged from the ledger alone — no provider call.

This is the preview `save_training_plan` reports after a save so the
athlete learns the calendar is behind, and the count `get_training_plan`
shows next to the calendar block.

create.description: Entries the ledger has no live row for.

remove.description: Live rows no entry wants any more.

unchanged.description: Entries whose live row already carries this content.

update.description: Entries whose content differs from the live row's.

RampUnmeasurable.description: Why a ramp check could not produce a verdict.

oneOf.description:
No cached activity in the window — no provider connected, a new
account, or a genuine layoff. There is no baseline to compare against.

The plan's first week carries no `duration_min` on any day, so its
planned hours cannot be summed.

RampVerdict.description:
What the ramp check concluded about a saved plan.

Serialised because the save reports it to the agent: the numbers are
descriptive magnitudes — planned hours, the athlete's recent average, the
fractional increase — and never a risk claim, which is the CI-enforced
framing rule for load ratios. The agent writes the sentence; this carries
only what was measured.

tools.name: push_training_plan
tools.description: Put the athlete's active training plan on their calendar provider (Intervals.icu today), or bring the calendar up to date after the plan changed: creates the days that are missing, updates the ones that changed, removes the ones the plan no longer has, and leaves alone any the athlete edited on the provider. Never touches dates before today. Call it when the athlete or coach asks to put or update the plan on their calendar — not on your own initiative after a save; save_training_plan's reply says when the calendar is behind. Requires a saved plan and a connected account of a provider that writes a training calendar. A group's human coach pushes a consenting athlete's plan by passing `athlete` from their own direct chat in Dravr, through the athlete's Intervals.icu link: the athlete must have allowed calendar writes on it, and Intervals.icu must list the coach as their coach. Only the published plan is pushed: a coach's unpublished draft never is, and the reply's unpublished_draft says when one exists.

Only the group's human coach (attached via a coach invite) may set it, for a consenting athlete in a group they coach who allowed their coach calendar writes, from Dravr's own app or channels and from a direct chat — never in a room. tools.name: recommend_plan_flavour
tools.description: Choose the training flavour an athlete should run this season and lay the season out. Call it once /season and /calibrate have run, passing what the athlete answered — weekly hours and sessions at minimum. The stored profile fills in training age, the devices they have thresholds for and their primary sport; the active plan fills in the goal race. Returns every flavour they can run ranked with the reasons and evidence behind each, every flavour they cannot run with the reason stated, how confident the rule is, and the season's phases laid backward from the goal on the skeleton that fits. Present the verdict in your own voice, confirm the inputs it echoes back, and save the outcome through save_training_plan, passing `verdict` and `inputs` through exactly as returned here, with selected_by rule for the first-ranked flavour or coach/athlete plus the reason for any other. This only recommends; it writes nothing.

event_class.description: The goal event. Omit to derive from the active plan's goal race. One of: run_5k, run_10k, half_marathon, marathon, ultra, crit, road_race, time_trial, gran_fondo, sprint_tri, olympic_tri, half_iron, ironman, open_water_swim, no_race.

measurements.description: What the athlete can steer intensity by. Omit to derive from stored thresholds; an athlete with none is read as effort. Entries from: lactate, power, pace, hr, rpe.

recovery_speed.description: From /calibrate RecoverySpeed. Masters-style loading triggers on this, never on age. One of: fast, typical, limited.

season_phase.description: Where in the season the athlete stands, if known. One of: off_season, base, pre_competition, competition.

tools.name: save_training_plan
tools.description: Persist the training plan you agreed with the athlete — the outline (goal race, strategy, the season phases, the flavour and who chose it, the season window) and/or day-by-day weeks (each may name the outline phase it instantiates, and each day the catalogue template it is built from with the values filled in) — in the SAME turn you state it. The plan is the athlete's one season, shared by every agent they use: weeks saved without an outline attach to it whoever laid it. Send an outline only for a season you laid, or when the athlete asked you to re-lay or change the outline of a season another agent laid — then set replace_season to true. Re-save a week another agent wrote only when the athlete asks for that change. Saved plans are re-injected into future conversations; an unsaved plan is forgotten. Adjustments re-save only the changed week(s) and supersede prospectively; past weeks stay immutable. For a day with interval structure, give steps (same shape as prescribe_workout's session.structure) — that is what puts workout-builder steps and a planned load on the calendar; prose alone reaches it as a timed entry. Saving never writes to the athlete's calendar: when the reply's calendar.stale is true, their Intervals.icu calendar no longer matches the plan — tell them, and offer push_training_plan only when calendar.pushed_by is absent; when it is human_coach, the athlete reads that calendar through their human coach's link, so tell them their human coach updates it. A group's human coach saving for a consenting athlete — `athlete` from their own direct chat, never in a room, or no `athlete` in the coach's thread about that athlete — writes the coach's draft of the athlete's plan: the reply says draft: true, and the athlete sees none of it, on their plan, calendar or agent, until the coach publishes it with publish_training_plan.

agent_id.description: The agent authoring this save, read only on a call with no conversation (a direct MCP call); a chat turn's own agent always wins.

athlete.description: Roster display name of the athlete whose plan this is. Only the group's human coach (attached via a coach invite) may set it, for a consenting athlete in a group they coach, and only from a direct chat — never in a room. In the coach's thread about one athlete it defaults to that athlete; elsewhere, omit it to act on your own plan.

goal_fact_id.description: Existing pillar Goal fact this plan serves, when known.

outline.description: The plan outline — the athlete's vision: goal race + strategy, optionally the season phases, the flavour and the season window. Required when creating a plan; omit to adjust weeks of the existing active plan. Re-sending an outline supersedes the athlete's current plan.

flavour.description: The flavour the season runs on, with who chose it. Omit for a plan laid out without one.

id.description: A flavour id from the training catalogue (polarized-classic, pyramidal-base, hvlit-foundation, …); the save refuses an id the catalogue does not hold and lists the ones it does.

inputs.description: recommend_plan_flavour's `inputs`, passed through exactly as the tool returned it, when it ran.

override_reason.description: Why a coach or athlete chose this flavour over the rule's proposal. Required for coach and athlete; omit for rule.

selected_by.description: Who chose it: rule (the selection rule's proposal, taken as is), coach, or athlete.

verdict.description: recommend_plan_flavour's `verdict`, passed through exactly as the tool returned it, when it ran. A rule selection must be the flavour it ranked first.

goal_race.description: The goal (A) race this plan builds toward.

discipline.description: Discipline: gravel, xco, road, trail run, …

name.description: Race name as the athlete calls it.

priority.description: A = goal race, B = tune-up, C = training race.

phases.description: Ordered season phases, from the season start (or now) through the goal race and any later peak. Omit for a short plan that has no mesocycle structure.

flavour_override.description: The intensity architecture this phase runs on when it differs from the plan's flavour. One of: polarized | pyramidal | threshold | lactate_guided | hiit_dense | hvlit.

hard_sessions_max.description: Most hard sessions a week in this phase.

intent.description: What this phase is for THIS athlete, in coach voice.

kind.description: One of: prep | base | build | specialty | peak | taper | race | transition | recovery.

loading_pattern.description: Load-to-recovery week pattern inside the phase, as "3:1" or "2:1".

Purposes: recovery | endurance | endurance_long | tempo | sweet_spot | threshold | vo2max_long | vo2max_short | sprint | neuromuscular | race_specific | brick | strength_aa | strength_max | strength_maint | plyometric | mobility | uphill | downhill.

discipline.description: Discipline: gravel, xco, road, trail run, …

name.description: Race name as the athlete calls it.

Prose alone reaches the calendar as a timed entry. Omit for a steady or unstructured day.

What a push would change, without the entry list.

this calendar (see [`CalendarBlock::pushed_by`]).

The athlete's human coach, through the link the athlete reads the
calendar by: only the coach writes it, from Dravr.

CrowdedWeek.description:
One week whose hard sessions sit closer together than its flavour allows.

Named rather than paired for the reason [`WeekReadiness`] is: a tuple
serialises positionally and the reader has to know which slot is which.
The check is flattened, so the kernel stays the one definition of what
"too close" means — including the minimum it applied and which gaps were
short.

oneOf.description: Every gap between hard sessions meets the minimum.
At least one gap is short.

short.description: The short gaps, in date order.

oneOf.description: Fewer than two hard sessions, or no flavour to take the minimum from.

reason.description: Why.

PlanSafetyReport.description:
What the two safety-shaped checks found in the weeks this save wrote.

A coach's save into their draft of an athlete's plan carries the same
report, measured on the draft view — the draft's outline over the
athlete's live weeks — so the coach hears of it before publishing puts the
plan in the athlete's hands.

The compliance rail has measured every saved week since it shipped and
reported into a log line no agent reads; the readiness rail the same. This
is the half that reaches the turn: the agent sees what the platform
measured on the save it just made, and can say so before the athlete acts
on a week that crowds its hard days or opens well above their recent load.

Only the two checks the ledger calls safety-shaped travel here. Time in
zone, volume against target and template parameter ranges are coaching
judgements the agent already owns, and a platform that volunteered those
would be second-guessing the plan rather than flagging a risk.

Structured, never prose. What the athlete is told is the agent's to write:
the framing rules on load ratios are CI-enforced and live in the prompt,
so a sentence composed here would be a second place they could be broken.

Absent when both checks read within, unmeasured, or had nothing to measure
— which is the common case and costs the turn nothing.

crowded_weeks.description: Weeks whose hard sessions are closer together than the minimum.

ramp.description:
The opening week against the athlete's recent weekly hours, when it
came in above the threshold. `None` when it did not, or when there was
no baseline to compare against.

PushPreview.description:
What a push would do, judged from the ledger alone — no provider call.

This is the preview `save_training_plan` reports after a save so the
athlete learns the calendar is behind, and the count `get_training_plan`
shows next to the calendar block.

create.description: Entries the ledger has no live row for.

remove.description: Live rows no entry wants any more.

unchanged.description: Entries whose live row already carries this content.

update.description: Entries whose content differs from the live row's.

RampUnmeasurable.description: Why a ramp check could not produce a verdict.

oneOf.description:
No cached activity in the window — no provider connected, a new
account, or a genuine layoff. There is no baseline to compare against.

The plan's first week carries no `duration_min` on any day, so its
planned hours cannot be summed.

RampVerdict.description:
What the ramp check concluded about a saved plan.

Serialised because the save reports it to the agent: the numbers are
descriptive magnitudes — planned hours, the athlete's recent average, the
fractional increase — and never a risk claim, which is the CI-enforced
framing rule for load ratios. The agent writes the sentence; this carries
only what was measured.

oneOf.description: The opening week sits within the threshold of recent load.

planned_hours.description: Planned hours in the plan's first week.

oneOf.description: The opening week exceeds recent load by more than the threshold.

planned_hours.description: Planned hours in the plan's first week.

superseded.description: Whether it replaced an earlier version of the same week.

week_start.description: The Monday the week starts on.

Unmeasured.description: Why a check could not be measured.

oneOf.description: The phase states no target for this check.
No flavour is on file to take the cap or spacing from.
No session in the week could be classified.
Fewer than two hard sessions, so there is no gap to measure.
No session carries or implies a duration.

calendar.description:
What a push would change now, when the calendar already carries this
plan. Absent when the athlete has never pushed — an athlete who does
not use the calendar is not nagged about it.

draft.description:
`true` when a group's human coach saved for a coached athlete: the
save went into the coach's draft, which the athlete does not see
until the coach publishes it with `publish_training_plan`. `plan_id`
is then the draft's.

goal_fact_id.description: The living goal fact the plan is anchored to, when one was recorded.

goal_race.description: The goal race, as name and date, for the reply to quote back.

ignored_arguments.description:
Argument keys the caller supplied that this tool does not have.

Serde drops an unknown key in silence, so a plan saved with
`agent_id` instead of `agent_id` stores against no agent and the
athlete is told "no active plan to extend yet" on some later turn,
with nothing anywhere naming the cause. Reporting the dropped keys
puts that on the turn it happened, where the model can fix it.

Reported rather than refused on purpose: these payloads are
LLM-written, and one provider wraps its arguments in an envelope of
its own (Cohere's v1 `{"parameters":{...}}` leaking onto the v2
surface), so rejecting an unknown key would turn a degraded turn into
a failed one — intermittently, and only on that provider.

Empty on every well-formed call, and then omitted from the wire.

What the two safety-shaped checks found in the weeks just written. On

weeks.

why this is a type rather than three call sites deciding for themselves:
`format=json` sends the tool's own shape, `format=toon` sends a compact
string envelope, and a TOON conversion that fails falls back to JSON while

`oneOf`, so the schema does not itself assert the arms are mutually
exclusive. A client tells them apart by the keys: `toon` and `result` are
the envelope's, and they are fixed rather than per-tool for that reason.

in a schema, so the old `result_toon` / `recipes_toon` / `recipe_toon` /

tool name already gives, and the contract is now expressible.

tools.name: set_physiology
tools.description: Save the athlete's physiological measurements — FTP, threshold pace, max, resting and threshold heart rate, lactate threshold, VO2 max, weight, age, sex — so training load, zones and every personalised calculation use their real numbers instead of generic per-sport estimates. Training load is scored against what is saved here and nowhere else — power against the FTP, heart rate against the threshold heart rate (estimated from the lactate threshold and max HR when none is saved) — in analyze_training_load, get_training_history, calculate_fitness_score, generate_recommendations and the recovery tools. Also saves critical power, W′, critical speed and D′, each with whether it was measured or estimated (measurement_kind) and by whom (measurement_source); an estimated value is quoted as an estimate with its source, never as a measurement. Call this whenever the athlete states one of these values, for example 'my FTP is 285' or 'my max HR is 190'. Pass only the fields they actually gave you; everything else keeps its stored value. The result is the profile re-read from storage after the write, so report back only what it contains.

critical_power_watts.description: Critical power (CP) in watts: the asymptote of the power-duration curve. Needs measurement_kind.

critical_speed_mps.description: Critical speed (CS) in metres per second, the running analogue of critical power: 4:00/km is 4.17. Needs measurement_kind.

d_prime_meters.description: D′ (D prime) in metres, the distance capacity above critical speed. Needs measurement_kind.

fitness_level.description: One of beginner, recreational, intermediate, advanced, elite, professional.

ftp_watts.description: Functional Threshold Power in watts. Saving it also derives and stores the athlete's power zones.

lactate_threshold_percentage.description: Lactate threshold as a fraction of VO2 max, between 0.65 and 0.95 (about 0.75-0.90 for a trained athlete), as a lab test reports it. It places threshold pace in the pace zones, and with max_hr estimates the LTHR when no threshold_hr is saved.

max_hr.description: Maximum heart rate in bpm. Saving it together with resting_hr derives and stores the athlete's heart-rate zones.

measured_on.description: The day the critical power, W′, critical speed or D′ in this call was measured or estimated, as YYYY-MM-DD, when the athlete or the source gives it.

measurement_kind.description: Required with critical_power_watts, w_prime_joules, critical_speed_mps or d_prime_meters, and applies to all of them in this call. measured only when the athlete names the test that produced the value (a lab test, a 3-min all-out test, time trials fitted to the model); estimated when an app or provider modelled it from training data, or the athlete gave the number without naming a test. One of: measured, estimated.

measurement_source.description: Who or what produced the critical power, W′, critical speed or D′ in this call: a provider or app (vekta, intervals.icu), a test (lab, 3-min all-out test), or athlete-reported when the athlete named no source. An estimate is quoted with it.

primary_sport.description: The athlete's main sport, e.g. run, ride, swim, trail_running.

sex.description: Physiological sex, only as the athlete states it: one of male, female. It selects the published equations that take one (Keytel's energy estimate, the sex-specific LT1 pace ratio); never infer it from a name. Omit it when the athlete has not said.

threshold_hr.description: Lactate threshold heart rate (LTHR) in bpm, from a 30-minute field test, a ramp test or a lab report. Heart-rate-based training load is scored against it.

threshold_pace_sec_per_km.description: Threshold pace in seconds per kilometre — the running equivalent of FTP. A 4:10/km threshold is 250.

w_prime_joules.description: W′ (W prime) in joules, the work capacity above critical power: 20 kJ is 20000. Needs measurement_kind.

oneOf.description: Intermediate athlete (2-4 years experience, local competition)

HistoryRefresh.description:
What happened to the athlete's stored daily rollup when the thresholds it
is scored against changed.

oneOf.description: The change moved no number training load is scored against.
No daily rows were stored, so none could be stale.
The stored days were recomputed against the saved thresholds.

Recomputing failed. `get_training_history` reads rows scored against
the previous thresholds until `compute_training_history` runs.

reason.description: Why, safe to relay to the athlete.

HrZoneModel.description: Which model cut a stored set of heart-rate zones.

oneOf.description:
Five zones at fixed fractions of heart-rate reserve, written before
the zones moved to cageux. Only ever read from an old row; nothing
writes it.

HrZoneSet.description:
Heart-rate zone boundaries for a single user.

Each `zN_max` is the upper bound (inclusive) of zone `N` in beats per
minute; zone `N+1` starts above it. `z6_max` is present when the athlete's
tier carries a zone 6 (`VO2max` of 50 or more and a zone 5 that stops
short of their maximum), and is then their maximum heart rate.

This is distinct from
[`pierre_core::models::HeartRateZone`](super::HeartRateZone), which carries
per-activity time-in-zone counts. `HrZoneSet` is the per-user definition;
`HeartRateZone` is the per-activity occupancy.

model.description:
Which model cut these boundaries. A row written before this field
existed reads as [`HrZoneModel::Legacy`].

tier.description: The `VO2max` tier that chose the zone fractions; absent on a legacy row.

vo2_max_source.description:
Whether the `VO2max` that chose the tier was the athlete's own or
estimated from their heart rates; absent on a legacy row.

z1_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 1 (recovery) in bpm.

z1_min.description:
Lower bound of Zone 1 (recovery) in bpm, inclusive: the zone's floor
on the athlete's reserve. Absent on a legacy row.

z2_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 2 (endurance) in bpm.

z3_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 3 (tempo) in bpm.

z4_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 4 (threshold) in bpm.

z5_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 5 (`VO2max`) in bpm.

z6_max.description:
Upper bound of Zone 6 (anaerobic) in bpm, the athlete's maximum heart
rate; absent when their zones have no zone 6, and on a legacy row.

HrZoneTier.description:
An athlete's `VO2max` tier, which selects the heart-rate reserve fractions
their zones are cut at

This is a cut on measured or estimated `VO2max`, not the athlete's declared
experience ([`crate::models::FitnessLevel`]): a self-described beginner
with a `VO2max` of 55 gets the advanced tier's zones.

oneOf.description: `VO2max` from 50 up to 60 ml/kg/min: zone 6 becomes available
`VO2max` of 60 ml/kg/min or more: the narrowest bands

MeasurementKind.description:
Whether a physiological value was measured or estimated.

This is what decides how the value may be framed. A measured critical
power is "your CP is 312 W"; an estimated one is "Vekta estimates your CP
at 312 W", never stated bare. Where the value came from is a separate axis
([`MetricProvenance::origin`]): a provider can hand over either kind.

oneOf.description:
Produced by a named test: a lab protocol, a 3-minute all-out test, a
set of time trials fitted to the model, a track test.

Produced by a model from training data (a provider's or an app's), or
stated by the athlete without naming the test behind it.

MetricProvenance.description: Where a physiological value came from and how much it can be trusted.

as_of.description: The day the value was measured or estimated, when known.

kind.description: Measured or estimated — the framing axis.

origin.description:
Who produced it: a provider (`vekta`, `intervals.icu`), a test (`lab`,
`3-min all-out test`), or `athlete-reported`. The attribution an
estimate is quoted with.

PhysiologicalSex.description:
An athlete's physiological sex, as the published equations use it.

Keytel et al. (2005) take it for exercise energy expenditure, and
Esteve-Lanao et al. (2026) give sex-specific VT1/VT2 speed ratios for the
aerobic-threshold pace.

It selects an equation's coefficients and nothing else. It is recorded
only when the athlete states it or a provider reports it, never inferred
from a name or anything else; absent, every reader falls back to the
pooled or sex-free form, or reports that it needs it.

PhysiologyProfile.description:
The athlete's physiological profile as the tools echo it back.

Every measurement is optional: a profile is built up over time, and an
athlete who has only ever given a resting heart rate has a profile with
one field set. Reporting the absent ones as absent rather than as zero is
what keeps an agent from reasoning off a fabricated number.

`fitness_level` and `primary_sport` are NOT optional — they carry their
own defaults — which is why they are the enums rather than strings.

critical_power_watts.description:
Critical power, in watts, with whether it was measured or estimated
and by whom. Quote an estimated value as an estimate, attributed to
its origin ("Vekta estimates your CP at 312 W"), never as a
measurement.

critical_speed_mps.description:
Critical speed, in metres per second, with its provenance. Quoted the
same way as `critical_power_watts`.

d_prime_meters.description:
D′, in metres, with its provenance. Quoted the same way as
`critical_power_watts`.

hr_zones.description:
Heart-rate zone boundaries, cageux's `VO2max`-tiered Karvonen zones
(zone 6 when the tier has one). Absent until both a resting and a
maximum heart rate are on the profile, because they are cut from the
reserve between the pair.

lactate_threshold_percentage.description:
Lactate threshold as a fraction of `VO2max`. Sets threshold pace, and
estimates the LTHR when none is measured.

power_zones.description:
Power zone boundaries, Coggan's seven levels from the FTP (zone 7 is
everything above `z6_max`). Absent for an athlete with no saved FTP.

primary_sport.description:
The sport the athlete mostly trains. Open-ended: a provider-specific
sport no enum anticipated arrives as `Other`.

threshold_hr.description:
Measured lactate threshold heart rate, in bpm — what heart-rate
training stress is scored against.

threshold_pace_sec_per_km.description: Threshold pace, in seconds per kilometre.

threshold_provenance.description:
Where `ftp_watts`, `threshold_hr`, `max_hr` and
`threshold_pace_sec_per_km` came from, for the ones a provider supplied
(`import_provider_thresholds`). Each listed value is that provider's
estimate: quote it with its origin ("intervals.icu has your FTP at
285 W"), never as a measurement. A threshold not listed is the
athlete's own, and the field is absent when all of them are.

w_prime_joules.description:
W′, in joules, with its provenance. Quoted the same way as
`critical_power_watts`.

PowerZoneModel.description: Which model cut a stored set of power zones.

oneOf.description:
Five zones at configurable FTP percentages, written before the zones
moved to cageux. Only ever read from an old row; nothing writes it.

PowerZoneSet.description:
Power zone boundaries for a single user (cycling / running power).

Each `zN_max` is the upper bound (inclusive) of zone `N` in watts, rounded
to the watt. Zone 7 is everything above `z6_max` and has no upper bound;
a legacy row holds only five zones and no `z6_max`.

model.description:
Which model cut these boundaries. A row written before this field
existed reads as [`PowerZoneModel::Legacy`].

z1_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 1 (active recovery) in watts.

z2_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 2 (endurance) in watts.

z3_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 3 (tempo) in watts.

z4_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 4 (lactate threshold) in watts.

z5_max.description: Upper bound of Zone 5 (`VO2max`) in watts.

z6_max.description:
Upper bound of Zone 6 (anaerobic capacity) in watts; zone 7
(neuromuscular power) is everything above it. Absent on a legacy row.

ProvenancedValue.description:
A physiological value together with its [`MetricProvenance`].

The pairing is the invariant: there is no way to hold one of these
values without saying whether it was measured.

as_of.description: The day the value was measured or estimated, when known.

kind.description: Measured or estimated — the framing axis.

origin.description:
Who produced it: a provider (`vekta`, `intervals.icu`), a test (`lab`,
`3-min all-out test`), or `athlete-reported`. The attribution an
estimate is quoted with.

value.description: The value, in the unit its field name carries.

ProvenancedValue2.description:
A physiological value together with its [`MetricProvenance`].

The pairing is the invariant: there is no way to hold one of these
values without saying whether it was measured.

provider, always [`MeasurementKind::Estimated`] with the provider as its
origin and the day the provider's setting last changed: the framing is

An import refreshes only an entry its own origin wrote, so a value the

anyOf.description: `format=json`, the default: the tool's own shape, unchanged.
`format=toon`: the payload rendered as one compact TOON string.

TOON was asked for and could not be produced. The payload still arrives,
as JSON, and says why it is not what was requested — a caller that
silently received JSON would parse it as TOON and fail further away.

format_fallback.description: Always true; present so the fallback is detectable on its own.

outputSchema.description:
A tool payload after the caller's `format` argument has been applied.

Which shape arrives depends on the REQUEST rather than the data, which is
why this is a type rather than three call sites deciding for themselves:
`format=json` sends the tool's own shape, `format=toon` sends a compact
string envelope, and a TOON conversion that fails falls back to JSON while
saying so. Untagged, so the derived schema is an `anyOf` over exactly
those three arms — schemars emits `anyOf` for an untagged enum, not
`oneOf`, so the schema does not itself assert the arms are mutually
exclusive. A client tells them apart by the keys: `toon` and `result` are
the envelope's, and they are fixed rather than per-tool for that reason.

The envelope keys are fixed (`toon`, `result`) rather than derived from a
per-tool `data_key`. A property name that changes per tool cannot be stated
in a schema, so the old `result_toon` / `recipes_toon` / `recipe_toon` /
`results_toon` spelling is gone — the key no longer carries information the
tool name already gives, and the contract is now expressible.
outputSchema.title: Formatted

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: Check a factual claim against the claim-verification pipeline (rhetoric → deterministic bounds → the athlete's own physiology → the athlete's own activity record → evidence corpus) and return a structured verdict with evidence strength and optional citations. Dravr checks the replies it writes in its own app and messaging; a reply an MCP client or agent writes from this server's data is checked only through this tool. Call it on every figure about the athlete (category athlete_data) before stating it, and on any physiological, nutrition, training, or supplement claim you are not certain about.

minimum_strength.description: Minimum evidence strength that counts as Supported. One of: strong | mixed | weak | none. Defaults to mixed.

outputSchema.description:
The structured verdict `verify_claim` answers with.

Both halves of the contract come from this type: `answers_with` derives the
declared `outputSchema` from it, and `execute` serializes an instance of it
as the payload. They cannot drift, because adding a field here changes both
and removing one stops compiling.

evidence_refs.description: Citations backing the verdict; absent when the layer that fired cites none.

evidence_strength.description: How strong the supporting evidence is.

explanation.description: Why the pipeline reached this verdict, in the agent's words.

layer_fired.description:
Which layer of the pipeline decided — `rhetoric`, `deterministic`,
`personalized`, `athlete_data` or `evidence`.

status.description: Whether the claim was supported, contradicted, or left unverified.

verdict_id.description: Stable identifier of the persisted verdict.

outputSchema.title: VerifyClaimResult
